description: Dillahunty argues that a preserved Gospel report alone establishes neither Jesus’s unity with the Father nor the occurrence and efficacy of supernatural forgiveness.
critique: Strongest feature: Dillahunty isolates the equivocation between transmission of a report and establishment of its supernatural content, answering Knechtle’s manuscript defense and appeal to Jesus forgiving sins. Principal limitation: Although “provide evidence to show that this happened” identifies the missing warrant, the reply never explains what evidence could demonstrate whether a sin was genuinely forgiven or establish Jesus’s relation to the Father. Live burden: He must articulate criteria for moving from testimony to theological actuality, then show why manuscript abundance, early dating, and patristic quotation cannot meet them without treating testimony as worthless. Locked score: The 86 reflects exceptional responsiveness and strong coherence, relevance, clarity, and charity, while weaker evidential warrant preserves the unresolved challenge of specifying confirmatory evidence for forgiveness itself.
